name: Hyper Yo-Yo craze
blurb: Ball-bearing trick yo-yos that swept Japan from 1997 and Chinese schools after 2006
title: Hyper Yo-Yo and the Yo-Yo Craze: Japan 1997, China 2006
description: The 1990s–2000s yo-yo craze: Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo swept Japan from 1997, and the 2006 Chinese TV series Blazing Teens did the same for China's schoolchildren.
h1: What was the Hyper Yo-Yo craze?
answer: The yo-yo craze of the late 1990s and 2000s was built on new trick yo-yos with metal axles or ball bearings that could spin ("sleep") at the end of the string for a long time. In Japan, Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line, launched in 1997 with licensed American brands such as Yomega and Duncan, set off a boom that lasted to about 2001. In China the peak came later, after Alpha Group's 2006 live-action TV series 火力少年王 (Blazing Teens) promoted its Auldey yo-yos to primary-school children. Yo-yos are still sold and played competitively today.

body: Older yo-yos had the string tied tight to the axle, so they could only go up and down. In 1990 the American SB-2 introduced an aluminium transaxle and became the first successful ball-bearing yo-yo; with far less friction the yo-yo keeps spinning at the bottom of the string, which makes string tricks possible.

ul: Sleeper: the yo-yo spins in place at the end of the string
Walk the dog: the spinning yo-yo rolls along the floor
Bind: a flick sends the yo-yo climbing back to your hand
String tricks: loops of string between the fingers that the yo-yo lands on

body: The Museum of Yo-Yo History cites Bandai as saying the Hyper Yo-Yo series has sold more than 30 million units worldwide. The popular Yomega Fireball sold for 2,200 yen in Japan in 1997.

火力少年王 was made by Guangzhou's Alpha Group, the company behind the Auldey (奥迪双钻) toy brand that had earlier sold four-wheel-drive racers, specifically to promote its yo-yos. It follows a group of teenagers training for a yo-yo tournament, and the yo-yos on screen were the ones in the shops. Many Chinese children who grew up in the late 2000s remember practising its tricks at break time. The show-plus-toy approach became Alpha Group's core business model.

Yes. Yo-yos never went away: there are national and world contests, Bandai released new Hyper Yo-Yo series in Japan in 2003, 2010 and 2024, and Blazing Teens yo-yos are still on sale in China. Original 1990s models are now collector items.

faq.a: It is a colloquial Chinese word for yo-yo; 悠悠球 is the other common name.

faq.q: When did Hyper Yo-Yo come out?
faq.a: Bandai launched the Hyper Yo-Yo line in Japan in 1997.
The string loops around a bearing or sleeve instead of being tied to the axle, so friction is low and the yo-yo keeps spinning.
